spec.name: Maximal Clique Enumeration
spec.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph, enumerate every vertex set that forms a clique and is not a proper subset of another clique.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.description: Return only maximal cliques at least this large.

problem_inputs.name: result_limit
problem_inputs.description: Maximum materialized cliques; a finite value permits an incomplete result.

required_outputs.name: cliques
required_outputs.description: Each returned vertex set is a distinct maximal clique meeting the size constraint.

required_outputs.name: returned_count
required_outputs.description: Number of materialized cliques.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: True only if all qualifying maximal cliques were enumerated.

optional_outputs.name: total_count
optional_outputs.description: Total qualifying clique count when enumeration completed or exact count-only continuation was performed.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate all inclusion-maximal complete vertex sets satisfying minimum_clique_size.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every materialized set must be exact; complete=true requires exhaustive enumeration.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: The same vertex set may appear only once.
solution_semantics.ordering: No clique or vertex ordering is semantically required.

validation_rules: Every pair of distinct vertices in each result has an edge.
No outside vertex is adjacent to every vertex in a returned clique.
For complete=true, results equal a trusted exhaustive oracle on tractable graphs.
edge_cases: An empty graph returns no cliques.
An isolated vertex is a size-one maximal clique when minimum_clique_size <= 1.
A complete graph has exactly one maximal clique containing all vertices.

correctness: set equality with oracle
duplicate count
invalid or non-maximal result count

required_outputs.name: induced_edge_value

solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Return one optimum unless tied solutions are explicitly added later.

Multiple distinct subsets may attain the same optimum.
An empty input graph has no feasible nonempty solution.

problems.name: Signed Network Structural Balance and Frustration Minimization

spec.name: Signed Network Structural Balance and Frustration Minimization
spec.problem_statement: Given a graph whose edges are each labeled positive or negative, determine whether it is structurally balanced (partitionable into two factions so every positive edge stays within a faction and every negative edge crosses factions), and when it is not, find a two-faction assignment minimizing the total weight of frustrated edges.

normalization: Every edge's type field must be exactly 'positive' or 'negative'; reject edges with any other or missing type.
Remove self-loops; a self-loop cannot be frustrated or unfrustrated under this definition.
Collapse parallel edges between the same pair only when they agree in sign; reject contradictory parallel signed edges between the same pair unless an explicit resolution policy is supplied.

problem_inputs.name: task
problem_inputs.description: Test exact structural balance via the cycle-based criterion, or find a minimum-frustration two-faction assignment.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Count frustrated edges or sum their declared nonnegative weights.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: balance_check is always solved exactly in linear time; frustration_minimization is NP-hard in general and approximate mode must disclose a bound.

required_outputs.name: balanced
required_outputs.description: Whether every signed edge can be satisfied by a two-faction assignment, independent of its cost. A zero weighted frustration optimum does not prove structural balance when zero-cost edges are allowed.

required_outputs.name: faction_assignment
required_outputs.description: Two-faction partition of every vertex realizing the reported frustrated_weight.

required_outputs.name: frustrated_weight
required_outputs.description: Total weight (or count, under weight_mode=unweighted) of frustrated edges under faction_assignment: positive edges crossing factions plus negative edges within a faction.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven for the requested task.

optional_outputs.name: frustration_optimal
optional_outputs.description: Whether the returned assignment minimizes frustration. A completed balance_check proves the decision, but need not minimize frustration when the graph is unbalanced.

optional_outputs.name: frustrated_edges
optional_outputs.description: Edges violating faction_assignment under the sign rule.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified bound or gap-to-best-known for an approximate frustration_minimization result.

solution_semantics.objective: balance_check decides whether a two-faction assignment satisfies every edge sign. frustration_minimization minimizes the cost of positive edges crossing factions plus negative edges within factions. balanced always refers to the sign-based decision, even when costs are zero.
solution_semantics.exactness: For balance_check, optimal=true certifies the balance decision, not a minimum-frustration assignment on an unbalanced graph. For frustration_minimization, optimal=true certifies the optimization under the declared numerical certificate; approximate mode must disclose approximation_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each vertex is assigned to exactly one of the two factions (A or B).
solution_semantics.ordering: faction_assignment is an unordered partition; the A/B labels are arbitrary beyond grouping and may be swapped per connected component.

validation_rules: Every edge's type in the normalized graph is exactly 'positive' or 'negative'.
frustrated_weight recomputes exactly from faction_assignment, edge signs, and (if weight_mode=edge_weight) edge weights.
balanced=true is independently verifiable via the standard cycle criterion: every cycle has an even number of negative edges.
balance_check always returns optimal=true.
edge_cases: An all-positive graph is trivially balanced by placing each connected component entirely in one faction.
A single negative edge between two otherwise-isolated vertices is trivially balanced by placing its endpoints in different factions.
Disconnected graphs: each connected component's faction assignment, and which label is 'A' vs 'B', is independent of other components.

A graph containing an odd negative cycle is structurally unbalanced. Its minimum frustrated weight is positive when all edge costs are strictly positive, but may be zero when a violated edge has zero cost.

correctness: balance-test agreement with the cycle-based oracle on small/medium fixtures
frustrated-weight recomputation
faction-assignment completeness (every vertex assigned exactly once)

spec.name: Transitive Closure and Reachability Indexing
spec.problem_statement: Given a directed graph, determine for queried vertex pairs whether the target is reachable from the source via a directed path, and optionally materialize or index full reachability to answer many such queries efficiently.

normalization: Collapse parallel directed edges between the same ordered pair to one edge.
Retain self-loops only insofar as every vertex already reaches itself by the reflexive convention; a self-loop does not change any reachability result.
Reject undirected input unless an explicit directed projection (both directions) is requested.

problem_inputs.name: query_mode
problem_inputs.description: Answer one (source,target) pair, a batch of pairs, or characterize reachability for every ordered pair.

problem_inputs.name: query_pairs
problem_inputs.constraints: required and nonempty for single_pair (exactly one entry) and batch_pairs
problem_inputs.description: List of {source, target} pairs to answer.

problem_inputs.name: build_index
problem_inputs.description: Whether to construct a reusable reachability index amortizing cost across future queries, versus a one-off traversal per query.

problem_inputs.name: enumerate_closure_edges
problem_inputs.description: For full_transitive_closure, whether to return every reachable (source,target) pair explicitly; only feasible when the result is small.

required_outputs.name: reachability_results
required_outputs.description: For single_pair/batch_pairs: {source, target, reachable} per queried pair, in query_pairs order.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every requested query (or, for full_transitive_closure, every ordered pair) was correctly resolved.

optional_outputs.name: reachable_pair_count
optional_outputs.description: Total number of reachable ordered pairs (including reflexive pairs); present for full_transitive_closure.

optional_outputs.name: transitive_closure_edges
optional_outputs.description: Explicit list of all reachable (source,target) pairs; returned only when enumerate_closure_edges=true and the result size is tractable.

optional_outputs.name: index_descriptor
optional_outputs.description: Opaque reference/metadata for a built reachability index, reusable by later single_pair/batch_pairs queries without rebuilding.

solution_semantics.objective: For each queried pair, determine whether target is reachable from source via a directed path of length >= 0 in the normalized graph (a vertex always reaches itself); full_transitive_closure characterizes this for every ordered pair.
solution_semantics.exactness: Reachability is always answered exactly; no approximate mode is defined for this problem.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: A repeated pair in query_pairs returns a consistent, identical result each time.
solution_semantics.ordering: reachability_results preserves the order of query_pairs.

validation_rules: Every reachable=true result is witnessed by at least one directed walk from source to target in the normalized graph.
Every reachable=false result has no directed walk from source to target, verifiable by exhaustive BFS/DFS on small/medium fixtures.
Every vertex is reachable from itself (reflexive case).
transitive_closure_edges, when returned, is consistent with reachable_pair_count.
edge_cases: source equals target returns reachable=true by the reflexive convention regardless of self-loops.
An edgeless graph has every non-reflexive pair unreachable.
Every pair of vertices within the same strongly connected component is mutually reachable.
full_transitive_closure on a graph where the closure is too large to enumerate must omit transitive_closure_edges and still return a correct reachable_pair_count with complete=true.

correctness: reachability agreement with exhaustive BFS/DFS oracle on small/medium fixtures
reflexive-case compliance
closure-edge-count consistency with transitive_closure_edges when both are returned
performance: amortized query time after index build

spec.name: Graph-Based Entity Resolution and Rule-Based Blocking
spec.problem_statement: Given a collection of candidate entity records and one or more declared blocking rules over record attributes, generate the reduced set of candidate record pairs worth comparing, and optionally confirm matches and merge them into resolved-entity clusters.

normalization: Treat every vertex as one candidate record; its attributes map holds the record's fields used by blocking_rules.
Input edges, if present, are treated only as known-coreference hints and are not required; a purely edgeless vertex collection is valid input.
Reject vertices missing any attribute field referenced by blocking_rules unless the rule declares that field optional.

problem_inputs.name: task
problem_inputs.description: Generate candidate pairs only, or additionally confirm matches and merge them into resolved entity clusters.

problem_inputs.name: blocking_rules
problem_inputs.description: Declarative predicates over a pair of records' attributes (e.g. field equality, bounded edit distance, shared token) whose disjunction defines candidacy.

problem_inputs.name: match_decision_rule
problem_inputs.description: Declarative rule or trained-model reference confirming whether a candidate pair is a true match.

problem_inputs.name: clustering_policy
problem_inputs.description: How confirmed match pairs are merged into final resolved-entity clusters when task=resolution.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: blocking is always exact given blocking_rules; correlation_clustering under resolution is NP-hard and approximate mode must disclose a bound.

required_outputs.name: candidate_pairs
required_outputs.description: Vertex pairs satisfying at least one blocking rule, each tagged with the satisfying rule id.

required_outputs.name: reduction_ratio
required_outputs.description: Fraction of the full pairwise comparison space (n*(n-1)/2) avoided by restricting to candidate_pairs.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every pair satisfying any blocking rule was found.

optional_outputs.name: resolved_entity_id
optional_outputs.description: Final entity cluster per record; present when task=resolution.

optional_outputs.name: match_decision
optional_outputs.description: Whether each candidate pair was confirmed a true match; present when task=resolution.

optional_outputs.name: evaluation_against_labels
optional_outputs.description: Precision/recall of candidate_pairs or resolved_entity_id against trusted duplicate labels, when available.

solution_semantics.objective: Produce candidate_pairs covering every pair satisfying blocking_rules while minimizing comparisons (maximizing reduction_ratio at full recall relative to the rules); for task=resolution, additionally confirm matches via match_decision_rule and merge confirmed pairs into resolved_entity_id per clustering_policy.
solution_semantics.exactness: blocking is exact and deterministic given blocking_rules; resolution's connected_components clustering is exact given match_decision, while correlation_clustering is NP-hard in general and approximate mode must disclose a bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each unordered vertex pair appears at most once in candidate_pairs even if multiple rules match it.
solution_semantics.ordering: candidate_pairs and resolved_entity_id are unordered.

validation_rules: Every pair in candidate_pairs satisfies at least one rule in blocking_rules when recomputed from the normalized vertex attributes.
No pair satisfying a blocking rule is missing from candidate_pairs (full recall relative to the declared rules).
reduction_ratio equals 1 minus |candidate_pairs| divided by n*(n-1)/2.
resolved_entity_id, when returned, assigns every vertex to exactly one cluster, and every pair with match_decision=true shares a cluster.
edge_cases: A record matching no rule with any other record forms its own singleton candidate set and, under resolution, its own singleton resolved entity.

Conflicting match decisions (A matches B, B matches C, but A does not match C) under clustering_policy=connected_components are resolved by transitive merging; correlation_clustering may instead keep them separate at some frustration cost.
An empty blocking_rules array is rejected as invalid input.
A fully connected candidate graph (every pair blocks) is valid but yields reduction_ratio zero.

correctness: recall of true-duplicate pairs within candidate_pairs relative to the declared rules (and trusted labels when available)
rule-satisfaction recomputation
resolved_entity_id cluster consistency with match_decision

spec.name: Null-Model Significance Testing via Degree-Preserving Graph Randomization
spec.problem_statement: Given an observed graph and a declared structural statistic, determine how unusual the statistic's observed value is by comparing it against its distribution over an ensemble of randomized graphs sampled from a declared null model, typically one preserving the degree sequence.

normalization: Remove self-loops unless the declared null_model explicitly permits them.
Collapse parallel edges to a single edge unless the null_model explicitly preserves multi-edges.

problem_inputs.name: observed_value
problem_inputs.description: The statistic's value on the real input graph; null means compute it directly from the graph using statistic_definition.

problem_inputs.description: Number of randomized graphs to generate for the null distribution.

problem_inputs.name: random_seed
problem_inputs.description: Seed for reproducible randomization.

required_outputs.name: null_distribution_summary
required_outputs.description: Mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum of the statistic over the sample_count randomized graphs.

required_outputs.name: z_score
required_outputs.description: (observed_value - null_mean) / null_std; null when null_std is zero.

required_outputs.name: empirical_p_value
required_outputs.description: Fraction of randomized samples whose statistic is at least as extreme as observed_value.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all sample_count randomizations were successfully generated and evaluated.

optional_outputs.name: null_distribution_samples
optional_outputs.description: Raw per-sample statistic values, when the sample count is small enough to return in full.

optional_outputs.name: randomization_diagnostics
optional_outputs.description: Acceptance rate, mixing, or other diagnostics for an MCMC-based null model.

solution_semantics.objective: Generate sample_count graphs drawn from null_model, each exactly satisfying its declared invariant, evaluate statistic_definition on each, and report observed_value's z_score and empirical_p_value relative to that null distribution.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every randomized sample must exactly satisfy null_model's invariant; the null_distribution_summary, z_score, and empirical_p_value are statistical estimates whose precision improves with sample_count, not exact quantities.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Not applicable.
solution_semantics.ordering: Not applicable.

gpu_limitations: GDlog: directed, at most 1024 vertices; GPU pairs checked by native reachability

operations.title: Count or list triangles
operations.description: Count three-vertex cliques of an undirected graph. Discard loops and collapse duplicate edges; weights are ignored. GPU enumeration uses native CPU materialization with count verification.

operations.title: Assign different colors to nearby vertices
operations.description: Proper greedy distance-1 or distance-2 coloring; no minimum-color claim. Undirected simple projection with isolates preserved. GPU colors the native C++ constructed distance conflict graph.

operations.title: Find the highest-value non-conflicting pairs
operations.description: Exact maximum-weight matching on an undirected graph, with no cardinality constraint. Require nonnegative weights; discard loops and keep the largest parallel weight. Preserve selected original edge IDs and return exact rational totals over admitted binary64 weights. Zero-weight edges may be omitted.

operations.title: Find the greatest bottleneck capacity from a source
operations.description: Exact max-min capacities with a predecessor witness, preserving direction. Every edge needs nonnegative capacity; loops discarded and largest parallel capacity wins. Zero is reachable. Source infinity and unreachable nulls have distinct flags.
